title: Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part IV)
gist: Teaser-only excerpt of Gavekal's Part IV asking whether US long bonds belong in a balanced portfolio. It recalls 2022, when the S&P 500 and 10-15-year Treasuries each fell about 20% under Fed tightening, and notes the Fed is starting another tightening cycle, but the argument itself is paywalled.

insights.claim: In 2022 the Federal Reserve's aggressive monetary tightening caused equities and bonds to sell off together: the S&P 500 fell about 20% while 10-15-year US Treasuries fell by a similar amount.
insights.speaker: Will Denyer
insights.so_what: Shows the stock-bond diversification failed when inflation and rate shocks drive both; the regime to watch for hedge reliability.

insights.claim: Because equities and long Treasuries fell together in 2022, balanced equity-bond portfolios performed very badly that year.
insights.speaker: Will Denyer
insights.so_what: Bonds only hedge equities when the shock is growth-driven, not policy-tightening-driven; check which regime you are in.
insights.quote: As a result, “balanced portfolios” of equities and bonds did horribly.

themes.theme: Renewed Fed tightening and bond hedge doubts

insights.claim: The author says the Fed is now starting another tightening cycle, which makes the idea of hedging equity exposure with bonds seem ludicrous on its face.
insights.speaker: Will Denyer
insights.so_what: The author frames the bond-hedge case as a hard one to make; the series presumably argues for it anyway, so watch later parts.
insights.quote: it may seem ludicrous to even entertain the idea of hedging equity exposure with bonds

insights.claim: Monetary tightening is not the only worry for bond investors today; the author points to further concerns covered in a separate piece on the challenges facing fixed income investors.
insights.speaker: Will Denyer
insights.so_what: Signals multiple headwinds for duration beyond Fed policy, such as supply or inflation; consult the cited companion piece.
insights.quote: monetary tightening is hardly the only cause for concern among bond investors today
